label: Requires the lack of: what a determination is makes its bearer not have every member of a set
term: requires the lack of (RequiresLack d S)
definition: RequiresLack d S: it belongs to what the determination d is that a bearer of d does not have every member of the set S. Examples: having exactly two units of extent requires the lack of having exactly three (S a singleton); a fixed capacity for two demands requires the lack of meeting three given demands together (no pair excluded). Non-example: knowing a truth requires the lack of nothing. It is not actual non-co-occurrence, not the incompatibility of two descriptions and not causal prevention. It is directed from d to S and need not be symmetric; nothing makes it monotone in S or irreflexive.
note: Stipulative analyst notion (#2145), attribution deferred. Lean has no declaration for it: it is a primitive parameter RequiresLack : D → Set D → Prop of TruthCore.Causality.RootPerfectionIntellect, constrained only by the open premises MemberGroundedAdmissibility and PureRequiresNoPureLack. Its applicability to the determinations of a simple source is open.
